newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks firm under foreign fund demand.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks firm under foreign fund demand.

text.p: Colombian stocks closed up driven by demand from foreign funds for shares in the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate.
Bogota's IBB index rose 1 percent to 1,047.09 amid a 1.8 billion peso volume while Medellin's IBOMED general price index gained 1.1 percent to 16,476.52 amid a 3.65 billion pesos trade.

"Foreign funds are not really bothered about the question of U.S. certification (of Colombia as a trustworthy ally in the global fight against drugs) but are going for solid stocks. On the whole they have a good perception of the economy and have faith and funds in it," a Bogota broker said.

One of the biggest gainers of the day was insurance company Compania Suramericana de Seguros, one of the flagships of Sindicato Antioqueno, up 2.8 percent in Bogota to 22,000 and up 3.27 percent in Medellin to 22,100.
Chocolate manufacturer Compania Nacional de Chocolates, head of the the Sindicato's food group, gained 2.93 percent to 9,500 on the Medellin exchange.
Cement maufacturer Cemento Argos, the Sindicato's leading cememt company, rose 2.06 percent to 7,400 in Bogota and 2.07 percent to the same price in Medellin.

"By buying Suramericana shares you're not just buying one share but a stake in 20 other companies including Argos and Nacional de Chocolates. Shares are scare and sometimes investors have to pay high to get their hands on them," another Bogota broker said.

As the flagship of the Sindicato, Suramericana has stakes in all the other companies of the Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate, made up of 250 individual companies with interests in food, finance, insurance and supermarkets.
Demand also spilled over to Banco Ganadero ordinary shares which gained 1.90 percent to close at 321 in Bogota and 1.56 percent to 320 in Medellin.
